title: Windows hook commands have no CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT fallback — contract enforcement silently vanishes on Windows hosts
scenario: The POSIX command uses ${PLUGIN_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}}, but commandWindows is `py -3 "%PLUGIN_ROOT%\taskplane\tp.py" screen` — cmd.exe has no default-value expansion, and Claude Code exports CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, not PLUGIN_ROOT. On any Windows Claude Code install the variable is unset, %PLUGIN_ROOT% stays literal, py exits with 'can't open file' — a non-2 exit code that Claude Code treats as non-blocking. Every PreToolUse screen (scope, read-only source protection, deny list, action budget), the dispatch check, and the SessionStart context hook fail open: a governed contract shows as active in tp status while nothing enforces it, which is exactly the silent-ungoverned state the screener's fail-closed design exists to prevent.
fix: Make commandWindows resolve both variables — e.g. `cmd /c "if defined PLUGIN_ROOT (py -3 \"%PLUGIN_ROOT%\taskplane\tp.py\" screen) else (py -3 \"%CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT%\taskplane\tp.py\" screen)"` — or ship a tiny screen.cmd shim in the plugin that picks the first defined root; apply to all three hook entries.

title: requirements.py writes the shared index.json unlocked and non-atomically while kb.py guards the same file with flock + atomic replace
scenario: kb.record_decision serializes on knowledge/index.json.lock and writes via tmp+os.replace (kb.py:44-80). requirements._save_index (requirements.py:60-63) writes the SAME index.json with a bare open('w') and takes no lock; record_requirement/record_debt/set_status all use it. During a parallel wave, a gate's kb.record_decision (plan approval, signoff) racing a `tp req debt`/`tp req new` does load→append→save on both sides: the second save silently drops the first's entry (a decision or requirement vanishes from the index while its .md file remains orphaned), two concurrent `req new` mint the same R-id, and any reader hitting the truncate-then-write window gets a torn index.json — kb.load_index raises ValueError and every loop-next kb.retrieve call crashes the step.
fix: Route requirements.py index writes through the existing kb machinery: wrap record_requirement/record_debt/set_status bodies in kb.mutate(ws) and replace _save_index's open('w') with kb._atomic_json (or move a shared save_index into kb.py and import it) — one lock, one atomic writer for one file.

title: Loop-authored specs/spec.md and init-authored .gitignore fail the execute gate's scope diff; recovery path is stated nowhere
scenario: Serial journey in /tmp/qa2-serial: tp init writes .gitignore, the pm step (whose own contract write_allow is specs/**) writes specs/spec.md, plan is approved, and the execute gate then fails with 'diff_scope: specs/spec.md is outside scope_paths' and the same for .gitignore — RUNTIME_OWNED exempts plan/ and .taskplane/ but not specs/, context/, docs/ or .gitignore. Committing the files does NOT clear it (the task contract snapshot predates the commit); the working recovery — commit, re-run `loop next` to refresh the contract snapshot, resubmit, gate — is named by no refusal and was found only by accident.
fix: Add "specs/", "docs/", "context/", "requirements/" and ".gitignore" to RUNTIME_OWNED (they are authored by the loop's own earlier steps/init), and extend the diff_scope error with the recovery: 'commit these loop artifacts, re-run loop next to refresh the contract snapshot, then submit and gate again'.

title: Single active-contract slot per workspace — parallel lens agents overwrite each other's contracts
scenario: This review's own 8-agent fan-out: each agent activated its read-only contract into the one active_contract.json; later activations clobbered earlier ones and one agent's clear released a sibling's contract (observed: task_ca285863 cleared while task_74dd430f believed itself active). Mid-wave, enforcement for 7 of 8 agents was void.
fix: Store contracts per task id (active/<task_id>.json); the PreToolUse screen resolves the caller's contract via TASKPLANE_TASK env passed in the dispatch brief, falling back to single-slot for compatibility. The dispatch briefs already carry unique task ids.

title: unittest runner bypasses store isolation: suite writes into — and deletes live governance state from — the developer's real ~/.taskplane (beyond the logged conftest artifact)
scenario: Ran `python3 -m unittest discover -s taskplane/tests -t .` at c8b6c9f: 478 tests ran, the real /root/.taskplane gained a modes/ directory (verified before/after), ~/.taskplane/projects now holds hundreds of test-created entries (prefixes -tmp-tp-sel-*, -tmp-tp-fix-*, -tmp-tp-prodgraph-*, -tmp-tp-governance-*, -tmp-tmp*), and this session's REAL active contract for /tmp/rel221 (task_8d3ceda5) was destroyed mid-review — its projects/ entry vanished after the unittest run, and `tp.py status` then reported 'no active contract'. Root cause: unittest never imports conftest.py and taskplane/tests/__init__.py is empty, so the docstring's 'belt' claim (conftest.py:8-10) is false and store-mutating tests operate on the real store. The known logged item covers the cosmetic runner failure; the real-store writes and cross-project state destruction are the un-logged consequence.
fix: Move the session-level `os.environ.setdefault("TASKPLANE_HOME", tempfile.mkdtemp(...))` into taskplane/tests/__init__.py (imported by both runners) and keep the pytest autouse fixture as the per-test layer; then the docstring's belt claim becomes true.

title: Deny-pattern matching is over-broad: raw substring on the whole command plus token-subsequence across command separators
scenario: With the default deny ["git push"], `screen_command` tokenizes the WHOLE command line and matches the pattern as a subsequence across separators (_token_subseq at line 510) or as a raw substring of the joined text (line 511). `git commit -m ok && echo push`, `grep "git push" docs/release.md`, or a Read-adjacent `echo "never git push"` are all denied — false denies that burn the worker's metered action budget (each deny still bumps the meter via _meter_bump(ws, tid, "denies") and, worse, confuses the agent into scope-escalation retries.
fix: Split the command on _CMD_SEP_RE first and match each deny pattern as a CONTIGUOUS token sequence at the head of a single segment (after _unwrap); drop the raw `pattern in joined` substring fallback.

title: Only-growing storage with no lifecycle: trace.jsonl, per-track gate artifacts, and abandoned per-project stores
scenario: Three stores grow monotonically with no TTL/archival: .taskplane/trace.jsonl (every event, forever), the store's artifacts/<track>/ gate snapshots (loop.py:2352-2356 re-dumps the whole graph per gate), and ~/.taskplane/projects/<key>/ which persists after its checkout is deleted (nothing ever prunes stores whose meta.json workspace no longer exists). On a machine used for many short-lived checkouts (worktrees, clones for review) the store directory accumulates dead per-project trees indefinitely.
fix: Add a `tp gc` (or an opportunistic sweep in `tp init`) that lists projects whose workspace_realpath no longer exists and offers age-based pruning; cap or rotate trace.jsonl (see SRE lens) and keep only the last N gate artifact snapshots per track.

title: mode.json (the private-vs-shared control file) is written non-atomically; a torn write silently drops the user's `private` flag
scenario: `set_mode` (line 1541-1583) writes each mode target with a bare `open(p,'w')` + `json.dump` (line 1560-1562) — no temp+os.replace. A crash/concurrent write mid-truncate leaves mode.json empty or malformed. `_read_personal_mode` (line 1466-1481) catches (OSError, ValueError) and returns `({}, found=False)` — i.e. treats a CORRUPT private setting as 'no setting recorded'. Resolution then falls through to a committed shared config or the plan default (`_persistent_mode`, line 1484-1520): a user who ran `tp share set private` can, after an ill-timed write, silently revert to the SHARED in-repo store, so their subsequent decisions/requirements get committed into `.taskplane-kb/` and pushed with the code. A privacy setting must fail safe (stay private), not fail open.
fix: Write mode.json (and the remote-keyed copy) atomically with temp+os.replace like every other state write in the kernel. Additionally, when `_read_personal_mode` encounters a file that EXISTS but won't parse, fail safe — treat it as private/unknown rather than 'not found' — so corruption never downgrades a private setting to shared.

title: Read-only contract screens `python -c` but not `python file.py` — the reviewed-source protection is escapable
scenario: A read-only review agent (e.g. a tp-lens dispatch) is given `write_allow=['.em-review/**']` plus the Bash tool. The read-only command path (lines 581-597) blocks concrete writes and every `opaque` mutator, but `_analyze` only marks an interpreter opaque when it sees an inline-code flag `-c/-e/-E` (line 462-468). `python3 file.py` (no such flag) yields targets=[] and opaque=None, so it is APPROVED. The agent (1) Writes `evil.py` into its allowed `.em-review/` dir — permitted — then (2) runs `python3 .em-review/evil.py`, whose body rewrites the reviewed source. The 'the reviewed source is protected (best-effort screen)' guarantee the read-only branch prints is defeated without ever tripping the screen. This is broader than the documented `python -c` build-contract gap: the read-only branch explicitly intends to block 'every un-screenable mutator', and a script FILE is exactly that.
fix: In the read-only COMMAND_TOOLS branch, treat any invocation of an `_INTERPRETERS` program as opaque='interpreter' when it has ANY non-flag file argument (not only `-c/-e`), since an arbitrary script body cannot be screened from argv. Simplest: under read_only, block interpreters outright (they are never needed for a review). Keep the existing `-c/-e` detection for build contracts.

title: Concurrency safety rests on Unix-only fcntl.flock while README advertises Windows - the guarantee silently vanishes there
scenario: The stdlib-only, no-server stance pushes all cross-process serialization onto advisory flock: _file_lock (taskplane_lite.py:1191-1206), loop.mutate (loop.py:198-210), kb.mutate (kb.py:60-80). Each wraps the import in `except (ImportError, OSError): pass`, so on Windows - which README.md:107 explicitly supports ('the `py` launcher on Windows') - every lock is a silent no-op. The exact failure modes these locks were added to fix (loop.py:185-190: 'a gated task silently reverts to running and the loop stalls'; kb.py:63-66: 'the second save orphans the first's decision'; the v1.5.2 dispatch-queue double-consume) are all live again on that platform, and neither README, docs/state-spec.md, nor the parallel-mode docs carry a Windows caveat. Choosing flock over a server/daemon is the right call for this project; shipping the degradation undocumented is the strain.
fix: Either close the gap in-stdlib - a msvcrt.locking branch in ONE shared lock helper (all three call sites currently duplicate the try/except; unify them) - or document the constraint honestly: 'parallel waves and concurrent teammates require a POSIX host; on Windows run serial loops only' in README and state-spec, with the fallback logging a one-time warning instead of passing silently.

title: Dispatch-audit queues silently truncated to the last 200 entries - the audit undercounts without saying so
scenario: _save_queue keeps `q[-200:]` (taskplane_lite.py:1219-1222) for expected_dispatch.json/observed_dispatch.json. dispatch_report is explicitly 'the by-hand trace.jsonl analysis, mechanized' (1267-1269) and `loop verify-dispatch` exits nonzero on mismatches - but on a long run (26-lens reviews emit 20+ briefs per wave; multiple waves easily exceed 200 events) the oldest unmatched expectations are silently dropped, so 'unobserved' and 'mismatches' undercount and the audit can report clean routing that never happened. The cap is a reasonable size/GC trade, yet it is uncommented and invisible to the report's consumer - an audit that silently forgets is worse than one that says it forgot.
fix: Name and surface it: comment the 200-entry cap where it lives, and have dispatch_report emit `truncated: true` (plus a note) whenever a queue is at cap, so verify-dispatch's numbers carry their own confidence bound. Revisit trigger: any run whose expected count hits the cap.

title: The screening hook has no failure-mode telemetry separating 'hook never ran' from 'hook approved'
scenario: cmd_screen fails closed on internal errors (good), but if the hook is not invoked at all — matcher regression, PLUGIN_ROOT unset so python3 exits 127, or the 15s timeout killing the process on a cold FUSE mount — the host default applies and NOTHING in .taskplane records that governance was absent for those actions. The dispatch check got exactly this observability (dispatch_report.hook_active, taskplane_lite.py:1267-1279); the primary enforcement hook did not. A post-incident review cannot prove the screen was live during a suspect action.
fix: Have `tp ready`/`tp status` compare the meter's last_seen_ts against the contract's activated_at and warn when a governed workspace shows zero screen activity — the cheap 'is the wall actually up?' probe, matching the pattern dispatch_report already uses.

title: budget_status treats a falsy ceiling as 'no ceiling' - --max-actions 0 silently creates an unmetered contract
scenario: budget_status does `if not max_a: return True, 'no action ceiling set'` (taskplane_lite.py:869-871) and build_contract coerces whatever it gets with int() (line 838). A user running `tp.py new --max-actions 0 ...` (intending 'no actions allowed' or just typo-ing) gets a contract the hook never meters - the one enforcement the docs call 'mechanical, before the action runs' is silently off, and cmd_new prints no warning.
fix: Validate in build_contract/cmd_new: reject max_actions <= 0 with an explicit error (or require an explicit --unmetered flag), and have budget_status distinguish None (unmetered) from 0 (exhausted).

title: Legacy-store adoption shutil.move()s a no-meta store unconditionally, risking a sibling project's KB on a slug collision
scenario: `_adopt_legacy_store` migrates a v0.9.6 pure-slug store to the collision-free key. When the legacy dir has no/unreadable meta.json it sets `owns=True` (line 1410-1411) and `shutil.move`s it into THIS project's new root (line 1415) — a destructive move, no copy/backup. Two projects whose paths differ only by punctuation share the same pure slug (the exact collision the hash key was introduced to fix). If the legacy slug store actually belonged to the sibling but predates meta.json, whichever project runs first STEALS and relocates it; the rightful owner then silently starts with an empty KB and its decisions/requirements/graph are gone.
fix: When meta.json is absent (ownership unprovable), COPY the legacy store into the new key and leave the original in place (or refuse and surface a one-line 'ambiguous legacy store — resolve manually' notice) instead of an unconditional move. Only `shutil.move` when meta positively confirms this workspace owns it.

title: Host detection (Codex/Claude/Tag) is re-implemented in three places with divergent results
scenario: The is-Codex probe `CODEX_HOME or CODEX_THREAD_ID` is copy-pasted in taskplane_lite._default_tier_models (1175), tp._onboard_report (115) and loop.user_summary (2288) — and only user_summary also knows the 'claude-tag' host (via store_env). If Codex renames an env var, or a new host (e.g. a CI runner) needs first-class treatment, three sites must change in lockstep; miss one and the surfaces disagree — onboarding says host=claude while tier routing still inherits Codex defaults, or model_for_tier sends 'haiku' to a non-Claude host, the exact cross-host model-id leak the tiering design exists to prevent.
fix: Add one kernel seam — tp.host() -> 'codex'|'claude-tag'|'claude' (env-injectable for tests, like user_summary's host param) — in taskplane_lite next to store_env(), and have all three call sites consume it.

title: A user's chosen 'private' data-residency setting can silently downgrade to the committed shared store
scenario: Store residency (private external ~/.taskplane vs committed in-repo .taskplane-kb) is the core privacy/data-location control. `_persistent_mode` (line 1484-1520) honors `private:true` only when `_read_personal_mode` returns found=True; any read miss — an unparseable mode.json (see data-safety finding 2), or a second clone of the same repo that never had a personal mode.json written — falls through to a committed shared-config store, moving future decisions into the repo. The remote-keyed fallback (_remote_mode_file) mitigates the second-clone case but depends on a git remote existing and on the earlier write having succeeded. Net: the decision that determines whether user knowledge is committed and pushed can flip from private to shared without an explicit user action, which is a data-residency/consent concern for regulated content.
fix: Make private the fail-safe default: when a personal mode file exists-but-unreadable, resolve to private rather than shared; write mode.json atomically (data-safety finding 2) so the private choice is durable; and when residency resolves to the shared store purely from inheritance/fallback (source != an explicit user setting), keep surfacing the existing 'team-visible' notice AND require an explicit confirmation before the first committed write.

title: trace() swallows OSError silently — the audit trail can stop recording with zero signal
scenario: The `except OSError: pass` at the end of trace() means that on a full disk, a read-only store, or a permission change, gate outcomes, hook denies, orphan releases and budget grants simply stop being recorded; a later incident review (`loop retro`, `verify-dispatch`) sees a clean-looking but truncated history and reaches wrong conclusions. Nothing distinguishes 'no denies happened' from 'denies happened but tracing was broken'.
fix: Emit one stderr warning per process on the first failed trace write (a module-level flag), so the operator learns the audit trail went dark without breaking the governed work.

title: FUSE tombstones and lock files accumulate in .taskplane and are never garbage-collected
scenario: On the unlink-refusing FUSE mounts safe_remove was built for (taskplane_lite.py:1090-1112), every contract clear leaves an `active_contract.json.removed.<pid>.<i>` tombstone; loop/kb/dispatch locking leaves `.lock` files behind (loop.py:198, kb.py:71). A busy loop clears a contract per step per task — over weeks the runtime dir fills with hundreds of stale files, inflating the dir-cache latency the same hosts are already slow on, and confusing anyone diagnosing state by listing .taskplane/.
fix: During activate(), opportunistically unlink (or safe_remove) `*.removed.*` entries older than 24h in the same directory — bounded, best-effort cleanup at a moment the workspace is provably being reused.
